html:
The Chisos were a Native American people of the desert where Chihuahua meets the Big Bend of the Rio Grande, in what is now Mexico and Texas. They were probably a branch of the Concho peoples.

Spanish records of the 1600s show them as hunter-gatherers who raided ranches and mission towns, sometimes with the Toboso. In the 1700s Apache bands moving south took over their range, and the Chisos disappear from the record, absorbed by the Apache or by mission towns. The Chisos Mountains in Texas probably keep their name. See also Chiso on the modern map.
